title_ar: حكم قراءة المأموم خلف الإمام فيما جهر به
title_en: The Ruling on a Follower Reciting behind the Imam in the Prayers Recited Aloud
body_ar: شيخي : سؤال عن حكم من يقرأ مع الإمام في صلاة التراويح و ذلك لتصحيح حفظه من القرآن .. و هل يتنافى ذلك مع عموم قوله تعالى : { و إذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له و أنصتوا لعلكم ترحمون } الجواب : نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه و سلم عن القراءة مع الإمام فيما جهر فيه و أذن في قراءة الفاتحة فقط و قد أخرج مالك في الموطإ عن ابن شهاب عن ا بن أكيمة الليثي عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انصرف من صلاة جهر فيها بالقراءة فقال هل قرأ معي منكم أحد آنفا فقال رجل نعم أنا يا رسول الله قال فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إني أقول ما لي أنازع القرآن فانتهي الناس عن القراءة مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما جهر فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقراءة حين سمعوا ذلك من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. و أخرج فيه أيضا عن العلاء بن عبد الرحمن بن يعقوب أنه سمع أبا السائب مولى هشام بن زهرة يقول سمعت أبا هريرة يقول سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من صلى صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن فهي خداج هي خداج هي خداج غير تمام قال فقلت يا أبا هريرة إني أحيانا أكون وراء الإمام قال فغمز ذراعي ثم قال أقرأ بها في نفسك يا فارسي فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول قال الله تبارك وتعالى قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرؤا يقول العبد { الحمد لله رب العالمين } يقول الله تبارك وتعالى حمدني عبدي ويقول العبد { الرحمن الرحيم } يقول الله أثني علي عبدي ويقول العبد { مالك يوم الدين } يقول الله مجدني عبدي يقول العبد { إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين } فهذه الآية بيني وبين عبدي ولعبدي ما سأل يقول العبد { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } فهؤلاء لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل. و أخرج فيه أيضا عن نافع أن عبد الله بن عمر كان إذا سئل هل يقرأ أحد خلف الإمام قال إذا صلى أحدكم خلف الإمام فحسبه قراءة الإمام وإذا صلى وحده فليقرأ قال وكان عبد الله بن عمر لا يقرأ خلف الإمام قال يحيى سمعت مالكا يقول الأمر عندنا أن يقرأ الرجل وراء الإمام فيما لا يجهر فيه الإمام بالقراءة ويترك القراءة فيما يجهر فيه الإمام بالقراءة .
body_en:
My Sheikh: a question about the ruling on someone who recites along with the imam in the tarāwīḥ prayer, doing so in order to correct his memorisation of the Qur'an. And does that conflict with the general import of the words of God, be He exalted: {And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may be shown mercy} (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:204)?

Answer: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade reciting along with the imam in the prayers he recites aloud, and permitted the recitation of al-Fātiḥah only.

Malik narrated in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn Ukaymah al-Laythi, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) finished a prayer in which he had recited aloud and said: "Did any of you recite along with me just now?" A man said: "Yes, I did, O Messenger of God." He said: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) then said: "I say to myself, what is it that I am being contended with in the Qur'an?" So the people left off reciting along with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in the prayers in which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited aloud, once they heard that from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him).

He narrated in it also, from al-ʿAlaʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yaʿqub, that he heard Abu al-Saʾib, the freedman of Hisham ibn Zuhrah, say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "Whoever prays a prayer in which he does not recite the Mother of the Qur'an, it is deficient (khidāj), it is deficient, it is deficient, incomplete." He said: I said, "Abu Hurayrah, sometimes I am behind the imam." He pressed my forearm and said: "Recite it to yourself, Persian. For I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: God, blessed and exalted, has said: I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves, half of it is Mine and half of it is My servant's, and My servant shall have what he asks. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Recite. The servant says {Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds}; God, blessed and exalted, says: My servant has praised Me. The servant says {the Merciful, the Compassionate}; God says: My servant has extolled Me. The servant says {Master of the Day of Judgement}; God says: My servant has glorified Me. The servant says {You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help}; this verse is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks. The servant says {Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those against whom there is anger, nor of those who go astray}; these are for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks."

He narrated in it also, from Nafiʿ, that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, when he was asked whether anyone recites behind the imam, would say: "When one of you prays behind the imam, the imam's recitation suffices him; and when he prays alone, let him recite." He said: and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar used not to recite behind the imam. Yahya said: I heard Malik say: The settled practice with us is that a man recites behind the imam in that in which the imam does not recite aloud, and leaves off reciting in that in which the imam recites aloud.

flags.arabic: و أذن في قراءة الفاتحة فقط … ويترك القراءة فيما يجهر فيه الإمام بالقراءة
flags.context: the Sheikh's opening sentence, set against the report from Malik with which the answer closes
options: the two are in tension and the text does not resolve it
the opening sentence states the general prophetic prohibition and its exception, and the closing Maliki report states the school's own practice, which does not take up that exception
the opening sentence is a slip for the Maliki position
flags.note: CRITICAL. The answer opens by saying that recitation of al-Fātiḥah alone was permitted behind the imam in the prayers recited aloud, and closes by quoting Malik that the follower leaves off recitation altogether in those prayers. That is the classic divergence between the Shafi'i and Maliki positions, and a reader will take whichever end of the text he reads last for the Sheikh's own view. He does not say in this written answer which he holds. Nothing has been resolved on his behalf; a reviewer or the Sheikh's office must say which is meant before this is displayed as a ruling.

flags.context: إني أقول ما لي أنازع القرآن
options: what is it that I am being contended with in the Qur'an?
why am I being disputed with over the Qur'an?
what is the matter with me, that I am being pulled against in the recitation?
flags.note: نازع here is the classical idiom for another voice pulling against the imam's recitation. The reading is uncontested in substance; the choice is only how much of the idiom to carry into English.

flags.context: عن ابن شهاب عن ا بن أكيمة الليثي عن أبي هريرة
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): the CMS text has a stray space inside ابن. Preserved in body_ar, silently correct in the English name, and recorded here rather than fixed in the Arabic.

translator_notes: The questioner asked specifically about reciting along in tarāwīḥ in order to correct one's memorisation. The Sheikh answers on the general rule for reciting behind the imam and does not address the memorisation motive, or tarāwīḥ as distinct from other prayers recited aloud. No application to that motive has been supplied.
Nor does he answer the second half of the question, whether the practice conflicts with Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:204. The verse is quoted by the questioner and not returned to in the answer.
The three reports are quoted from al-Muwaṭṭaʾ and the attribution is kept exactly as he gives it. He supplies no grading for any of them, and none has been added.
Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
